'''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|en|Fujiwara clan|qid=Q641628|lt=Fujiwara clan}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hok-ke|en|Fujiwara Hok-ke|qid=Q2975268|lt=Fujiwara Hokke}} {{ill|Q11655354|ja|閑院流|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanin lineage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11655354}} and its {{ill|Q11447787|ja|嫡流|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main lineage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11447787}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}<ref name="lib.u-tokyo">{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}</ref>{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|en|Kuge|qid=Q1196276|lt=Kuge}} was {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|en|Kazoku|qid=Q241734|lt=Kazoku}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Duke|en|Duke|qid=Q166886|lt=Duke}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|karahanamon|ja|唐花紋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karahana crest|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q21550705}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|en|Sanjō Sanetomi|qid=Q516646|lt=Sanjō Sanetomi}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō-daijin|en|Daijō-daijin|qid=Q1157586|lt=Daijō Daijin}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|af|Meiji-restourasie|als|Meiji-Restauration|an|Restauración Meichi|anp|मेइद्ज़ी कृंति|ar|استعراش مييجي|arz|استعادة مييچى|as|মেইজি To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ōgimachisanjō family|ja|正親町三条家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogyū-Sanjō family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11545676}} (later the {{ill|Ōgimachisanjō family|ja|嵯峨家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 正親町三条家|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11545676}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. 

== History ==

=== Heian Period ===
The {{ill|Q11655354|ja|閑院流|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanin lineage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11655354}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|en|Fujiwara no Tadahira|qid=Q1397601|lt=Fujiwara no Tadahira}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|en|Fujiwara no Morosuke|qid=Q325207|lt=Fujiwara no Morosuke}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinsue|en|Fujiwara no Kinsue|qid=Q3090629|lt=Fujiwara no Kinnori}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. 

His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kinnari|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11623074}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|qid=Q60949|lt=Emperor Shirakawa}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanesue|ja|藤原実季|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11623175}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|en|Emperor Toba|qid=Q349284|lt=Emperor Toba}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinzane|fa|فوجیوارا نو کینزانه|ja|藤原公実|pt|Fujiwara no Kinzane|zh|藤原公實|qid=Q10514083}}, fathered {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamako|en|Fujiwara no Tamako|qid=Q900258|lt=Empress Taiken-mon In}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|azb|سوتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Сутоку|ca|Sutoku|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوتۆکو|cs|Sutoku|de|Sutoku|es|Sutoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوتوکو|fr|Sutoku|hak|Sutoku Thiên-fòng|he|סוטוקו|id|Kaisar Sutoku|it|Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|ko|스토쿠 천황|mr|सुतोकु|nl|Sutoku|pl|Sutoku|pt|Sutoku|ru|Император Сутоку|sh|Car Sutoku|simple|Sutoku|sv|Sutoku|sw|Sutoku wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิซูโตกุ|tl|Emperador Sutoku|tr|Sutoku|uk|Імператор Сутоку|vi|Thiên hoàng Sutoku|yo|Emperor Sutoku|zh|崇德天皇|zh_min_nan|Sutoku Thian-hông|qid=Q349287|lt=Emperor Sutoku}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|2=ja|3=後白河天皇|qid=Q317984|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|2=ja|3=後白河天皇|qid=Q317984|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Consort kin|ja|外戚|ko|외척|vi|Ngoại thích|zh|外戚|qid=Q1050320|lt=Emperor's maternal relatives}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. 

The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Saneyuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11355837}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kiminori|ja|三条公教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Kinari|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11355816}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō-daijin|en|Daijō-daijin|qid=Q1157586|lt=Daijō Daijin}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. 

His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Sanefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11355831}}, attained the position of {{ill|Minister of the Left|en|Minister of the Left|qid=Q949008|lt=Minister of the Left}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. 

=== Kamakura to Edo Period ===
The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō-daijin|en|Daijō-daijin|qid=Q1157586|lt=Daijō Daijin}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|qid=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}.
